insights.claim: Neither the prediction nor the training FastAPI server registers authentication middleware, leaving all 24 HTTP endpoints unauthenticated at the application layer and relying entirely on platform-level network isolation for access control.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer detected no auth middleware on the FastAPI application. Source inspection of the app initialization confirms no add_middleware or Depends-based security is registered. The training server also has no auth. The inter-service model download path uses plain HTTP without authentication. For a component that ingests telemetry data and serves predictions that influence scheduling decisions, the absence of application-level authentication means access control depends entirely on Kubernetes NetworkPolicy or service mesh authorization.

insights.claim: The prediction server uses a background thread polling pattern with timestamp-based change detection to synchronize ML model artifacts from the training server, creating a tightly coupled intra-component dependency over plain HTTP.
insights.reasoning: The ModelSyncer class runs a background thread that polls training-service every MODEL_SYNC_INTERVAL_SEC (default 10s), checking /model/{name}/info for timestamp freshness and downloading via /model/{name}/download with streaming. This polling pattern means the prediction server cannot serve accurate predictions until the training server has produced its first model, and model staleness is bounded by the sync interval. The HTTP session includes retry logic for transient errors but no circuit breaker.
